chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Faddal and Al-Hajjal, all of them, from Th'labah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Maslamah al-Jariri, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'They reproach us and belie us, saying that we claim that two cries will occur. They ask,

Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: "So is one who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who does not go aright unless he is guided? What then is the matter with you; how do you judge?"

key_terms.أَفَمَنْ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ: So is one who guides to the truth

ai.seo_question: How to distinguish the true and false cries (Sayhah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) addresses the theological concern of distinguishing the true divine cry (*al-Sayhah al-Muhiqqah*) from the false one by linking recognition to prior faith. He cites Surah Yunus (10:35) to establish that those who already believe in the truth will naturally recognize its authentic voice, as the one who guides to truth is more worthy of following than the one who requires guidance. This highlights the Shia principle that *iman* (faith) serves as the epistemological key to verifying eschatological signs.

en.hubeali: H 14700 – Abu Ali Al-Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbaar, from Ibn Fazzaal and Al-Hajjaal, from Sa’albat, from Abdul Rahmaan Bin Muslama Al-Jariry who said:

I said to Abu Abdullahasws: ‘They reproach us and belie us that we are saying that the two ‘announcements’ which are to occur. They are saying, ‘How would we differentiate between the true one from the false one, if we were to be there?’ Heasws said: ‘So what do you respond to them with?’ I said, ‘We do not respond to them with anything’. Heasws said: ‘Say to them, ‘Those who believed in it from before (have faith) would recognise it. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Says:
“[10:35] Is He then Who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who himself does not go aright unless he is guided? What then is the matter with you; how do you judge?”
en.sarwar: 252. Abu Ali Al-Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbaar, from Ibn Fazzaal and Al-Hajjaal, from Sa’albat, from Abdul Rahmaan Bin Muslama Al-Jariry who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (a.s.): ‘They reproach us and belie us that we are saying that the two ‘announcements’ which are to occur. They are saying, ‘How would we differentiate between the true one from the false one, if we were to be there?’ He (a.s.) said: ‘So what do you respond to them with?’ I said, ‘We do not respond to them with anything’. He (a.s.) said: ‘Say to them, ‘Those who believed in it from before (have faith) would recognise it.

Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic Says: “[10:35] Is He then Who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or he who himself does not go aright unless he is guided? What then is the matter with you; how do you judge?”
